ArchitectureNotes.objective: Preserve exact Vast rules behavior while making browser runtime, replay evidence, and future AI bot integration easier to reason about and verify.
ArchitectureNotes.non-goal: Do not ship five-player support until Thief mechanics, setup, UI, serialization, and verification are implemented together.
ArchitectureNotes.risk-1: Rules logic, browser presentation, and bot decision boundaries currently span multiple files and can drift without explicit contracts.
ArchitectureNotes.risk-2: Future AI quality will remain capped if host simulation and legal-action extraction are not made deterministic and inspectable.

M-VAST-THIEF-SUPPORT.NAME: VastThiefSupport

contract.purpose: Introduce Thief as a supported fifth-player faction without regressing current four-player gameplay.

export-Thief.PURPOSE: Fifth-player faction support surface, currently partially wired through setup and basic turn actions.

export-ThiefPlayer.PURPOSE: Runtime state for Thief stats, action cubes, carried loot, stashed loot, path, and per-turn targeting.

M-VAST-THIEF-SUPPORT.depends: M-VAST-RULES, M-VAST-GAME, M-VAST-META, M-VAST-UI, M-VAST-SERIALIZE, M-VAST-BOT, M-VAST-HOST

notes.note-1: Keep four-player setup valid while explicitly preparing the engine for a fifth role.
notes.note-2: Execute Thief support as vertical slices: GRACE refresh, minimal five-player boot, core turn loop, loot/vault/stash, player interactions, cross-faction integration, then serialization/UI/host completion.
notes.note-3: Use placeholder browser presentation until final Thief art assets are available; placeholder UI must still expose gameplay state clearly.
notes.checkpoint-2026-04-27: Partial implementation exists in `vast/game.scala`, `vast/meta.scala`, `vast/ui.scala`, and `vast/VastHost.scala`: five-player validation, Vault tile inclusion, `ThiefPlayer`, Entrance setup, basic stat/action-cube turn flow, movement, dark-tile reveal choice, Loot, Pick Lock, carried/stashed loot, six-stash victory, and status UI. Host evidence reached `[VastThief][enable]`, `[VastThief][turn]`, and `[VastThief][loot]` markers before exposing remaining cross-faction gaps.
notes.blocker-2026-04-27: `vast.Game.performInternal` is near the JVM per-method bytecode limit and hit `Method too large` when additional Thief cross-faction cases were added directly. Next implementation must extract faction/action dispatch helpers instead of adding more cases to the monolithic match.
notes.next-step: Before adding Pickpocket/Backstab/full cross-faction behavior, refactor `performInternal` into smaller faction dispatch sections or route new action families through helper methods. Then rerun compile, fastOptJS, host round-trip, and Composer browser smoke.
notes.checkpoint-2026-04-28: Refactor wave 1 extracted Thief helpers to `vast/game-thief.scala` and setup helpers to `vast/game-setup.scala` using self-typed traits mixed into `Game`. Public action shapes remain in `vast/game.scala`; behavior is intended to be unchanged.
notes.checkpoint-2026-04-28-wave2: Refactor wave 2 split the monolithic `Game.performInternal` match: arms from Goblins through `SelfPerform` live in `performInternalPart2` in `vast/game.scala`; prior arms stay in `performInternal`, delegating unknown actions to part 2. Intended behavior-preserving; verification: `sbt compile`, `fastOptJS`, Vast sim.
notes.checkpoint-2026-04-28-wave3: Refactor wave 3 split `performInternalPart2` at the Dragon section: Goblins-only arms stay in part 2; Dragon through `SelfPerform` move to `performInternalPart3` in `vast/game.scala` (bytecode / maintainability, behavior-preserving).
notes.checkpoint-2026-04-28-wave4: Wave 4 moves Dragon `PartialFunction` dispatch from `caveTailPart3`/`performInternalPart3` into `vast/game-dragon.scala` as `GameDragonSupport#dragonDispatchPart3`; `caveTailPart3` retains Cave, Thief hooks, and board helpers. Call sites pass implicit `Game` for `GameImplicits` faction→player enrichment.

DF-START-BROWSER.NAME: Browser startup and Vast boot
DF-START-BROWSER.step-1: `hrf.scala` loads resources and discovers registered game metadata.
DF-START-BROWSER.step-2: `vast.Meta` validates faction combination and creates the `Game` instance.
DF-START-BROWSER.step-3: `vast.UI` attaches browser panes and renders the initial cave state.
DF-START-BROWSER.evidence: Successful `sbt fastOptJS`, local HTTP serve, and a browser smoke run that reaches a playable initial board.

DF-RESOLVE-TURN.NAME: Resolve a player turn
DF-RESOLVE-TURN.TRIGGER: Human or bot chooses a legal action
DF-RESOLVE-TURN.step-1: The acting faction receives legal actions from the current `Continue` state.
DF-RESOLVE-TURN.step-2: `vast.Game` applies rule-specific transitions and emits the next `Continue`.
DF-RESOLVE-TURN.step-3: `vast.UI` updates rendered state while preserving hidden information and legal selection affordances.
DF-RESOLVE-TURN.evidence: Targeted mechanic checks plus browser scenario validation for asymmetric faction actions and victory progress.

DF-SERIALIZE-REPLAY.NAME: Serialize and replay action stream
DF-SERIALIZE-REPLAY.step-2: The string is parsed back into an action.
DF-SERIALIZE-REPLAY.step-3: The replayed action remains semantically equivalent and does not diverge from the intended game transition.
DF-SERIALIZE-REPLAY.evidence: Round-trip checks and failure artifacts captured by host-side simulation code.

DF-BOT-DECISION.NAME: Bot selects a legal move
DF-BOT-DECISION.step-1: The host or runtime collects legal `UserAction` values for the current faction.
DF-BOT-DECISION.step-3: The selected action is applied through the same game engine as human moves.
DF-BOT-DECISION.evidence: Simulation runs complete without illegal-action divergence and produce stable result distributions.

DF-RULES-ALIGNMENT.NAME: Align implementation with XML rules
DF-RULES-ALIGNMENT.step-1: Relevant `rules/*.xml` topics are identified for the mechanic under change.
DF-RULES-ALIGNMENT.step-2: The corresponding code path in `vast/game.scala` and related UI/bot/serialization code is reviewed.
DF-RULES-ALIGNMENT.step-3: Verification scenarios are updated so future work keeps the rule and code in sync.
DF-RULES-ALIGNMENT.evidence: Named verification scenarios referencing both the rules corpus and the implementation modules.

DF-ENABLE-THIEF.NAME: Enable Thief as the fifth player
DF-ENABLE-THIEF.TRIGGER: Implementation wave for Thief support begins
DF-ENABLE-THIEF.step-1: `rules/thief.xml` is treated as the contract reference for setup, actions, scoring, and interactions.
DF-ENABLE-THIEF.step-2: `vast.Game` and `vast.Meta` are updated to allow a five-player composition that includes Thief.
DF-ENABLE-THIEF.step-3: `vast.UI`, serialization, host simulation, and bots are extended so Thief can participate without special-case breakage.
DF-ENABLE-THIEF.evidence: Five-player startup succeeds, Thief-specific actions are legal and replayable, and four-player regression checks still pass.

Phase-1.name: Baseline governance
Phase-1.goal: Make the current Vast architecture explicit and navigable before deeper feature work.
Phase-1.step-1: Anchor the XML rule corpus as a first-class reference.
Phase-1.step-2: Document the core rules engine as the authority for state transitions.
Phase-1.step-3: Document replay and action-transport stability requirements.

Phase-2.name: Runtime and UX verification
Phase-2.goal: Stabilize browser startup and high-value gameplay interaction surfaces.
Phase-2.step-1: Document faction validation and asset/runtime binding.
Phase-2.step-2: Document the rendering and click-path surface that must stay aligned with rules.
Phase-2.step-3: Document browser bootstrap files needed for launch.

Phase-3.name: Bot strength and AI readiness
Phase-3.goal: Prepare a safer surface for stronger bot play and future AI agent integration.
Phase-3.step-1: Document current heuristic bots and identify evaluation seams.
Phase-3.step-2: Document the host/simulation path for batch validation and future AI benchmarking.

Phase-4.name: Thief enablement
Phase-4.goal: Implement and verify Thief as the fifth supported player role.
Phase-4.step-1: Refresh GRACE artifacts and map `rules/thief.xml` to concrete execution slices.
Phase-4.step-2: Expand faction validation and setup from four-player-only to verified five-player support while preserving four-player starts. Current code allows 5p with Thief and keeps quick play 4p, but the latest post-filter compile still needs to be rerun.
Phase-4.step-3: Add minimal `ThiefPlayer` setup, Entrance placement, basic stats, action cubes, and placeholder status UI. Implemented at checkpoint, pending final verification after the last documentation/filter changes.
Phase-4.step-4: Implement the Thief core turn loop: stat assignment, movement, dark-tile peek/reveal, end-turn cleanup, and death basics. Basic flow exists; full death reward/respawn semantics remain pending.
Phase-4.step-5: Implement Loot, Pick Lock, Vault, carried/stashed loot, Dragon Gem handling, treasure shortage, and six-stash victory. Basic Loot/Pick Lock/stash/victory exists; treasure shortage and upgrade-space details remain pending.
Phase-4.step-6: Implement Pickpocket, Backstab, Stealth targeting, target-once-per-turn tracking, and Unnatural Evasion. Blocked on extracting action dispatch from `performInternal` to avoid JVM `Method too large`.
Phase-4.step-7: Integrate cross-faction rules for Knight, Goblins, Dragon, and Cave interactions with Thief. Temporary generation filters exclude some old cross-faction actions from targeting Thief until handlers can be added outside the monolithic match.
Phase-4.step-8: Complete browser status/overlay and interaction support for the fifth faction with placeholder assets. Status UI exists; board/overlay art remains placeholder.
Phase-4.step-9: Verify new Thief external actions serialize and parse through replay paths. Host round-trip reached Thief markers before cross-faction gaps; rerun after dispatch refactor.
Phase-4.step-10: Add legal-action-safe Thief bot behavior for host simulation. Generic bot can choose legal actions, but no Thief-specific evaluator exists yet.
Phase-4.step-11: Include five-player Thief scenarios in host-side simulation and round-trip checks. Host run exercises Thief setup/turn/loot/stash, then exposes remaining cross-faction blockers.

ExecutionPolicy.worker-owns: Only approved Vast-related source files, browser-launch files, and nearby verification artifacts inside the declared write scope.
